scenes.title: 1. Experimental Apparatus Setup
scenes.caption: The SoFIE chamber is mounted inside the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR). A 0.5 mm thick PMMA solid polymer specimen is installed inside a 100 mm flow duct with controlled oxidizer flow.

scenes.title: 2. Flight Sequence & Flame Pulsation
scenes.caption: In microgravity without buoyant updraft, the burning specimen draws fresh oxygen via vapor expansion. The flame periodically brightens (0.2s interval) as oxygen is drawn in, followed by dimming as local fuel accumulates.

scenes.title: 3. Observed Scientific Findings
scenes.caption: Under Exploration Atmospheres (elevated O2 at 34%, reduced pressure at 56 kPa), thick PMMA flammability boundaries expand substantially. Extinction limits shift to significantly lower air velocities than predicted by 1g buoyancy models.

scenes.title: 4. Scientific Boundaries & Limitations
scenes.caption: NASA Caution: All recorded data represents orbital 0g microgravity. Do not extrapolate quantitatively as a predictive model for Lunar (0.16g) or Martian (0.38g) partial-gravity environments without dedicated reduced-gravity testing.

scenes.title: 1. Cygnus Flight Flow Tunnel
scenes.caption: The Saffire experiment was conducted inside the Cygnus OA-5 cargo vehicle after departing ISS. Fans provided 20 cm/s forced ventilation across a large 0.4 m x 1.0 m solid SIBAL fabric.

scenes.title: 2. Steady Flame Propagation
scenes.caption: Unlike small 1g tests where convective buoyancy causes rapid upward spread, large-scale microgravity flame spread proceeds steadily under forced airflow, burning for over 8 minutes continuously.
